Souper Cubes vs Walfos Silicone Freezer Trays: Which Meal Prep System Actually Saves You Money?

Souper Cubes ($78.99) is the premium name in silicone freezer molds — the one you see all over TikTok and Instagram. Walfos ($25) is the Amazon bargain alternative that promises similar results for 68% less. We put both head-to-head to find out if the hype is worth the premium.

Published July 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data

Meal prep freezer molds are having a moment. Silicone trays that let you freeze individual portions of soup, sauce, rice, and proteins — then pop them out like ice cubes — have become the secret weapon of serious meal preppers. And the two names you'll see most often are Souper Cubes and Walfos.

Souper Cubes is the original, the internet-famous brand that went viral for good reason. Walfos is the most popular budget alternative, promising the same core functionality at a fraction of the price. The question is simple: does Souper Cubes justify costing more than three times as much?

Quick Verdict

Buy Souper Cubes (our pick) if: You meal prep in serious volume, freeze soups and stocks weekly, and want a set that will genuinely last for years. The platinum-cured silicone, steel-reinforced rims, precise fill lines, and tight-sealing lids are worth the money for heavy users. This is a buy-it-for-life kitchen tool.

Buy Walfos if: You're new to meal prep, want to try the concept without a big investment, or only freeze things occasionally. The Walfos trays work well for the price and will give you a solid year or two of service before the silicone starts to wear.

Our pick: Souper Cubes. The quality difference is real — thicker silicone, better lids, steel reinforcement, and precise 1-cup portions with fill lines. For serious meal preppers, the extra $54 buys you years of additional use. But the Walfos set is a perfectly good starter kit.

Where Souper Cubes Wins

The silicone is genuinely better. This isn't marketing fluff. Platinum-cured silicone is a fundamentally different material from standard food-grade silicone. It's denser, more durable, doesn't absorb odors (your Souper Cubes won't smell like last week's chili forever), and won't degrade or stiffen after repeated freeze-thaw cycles. After two years of weekly use, Souper Cubes still feel like new. Walfos trays will start showing wear after about a year.

Steel-reinforced rims solve a real problem. If you've ever tried to carry a silicone mold full of liquid hot soup to the freezer, you know the struggle — the walls flop, the contents slosh, and you pray nothing spills. Souper Cubes' steel-reinforced rims keep the shape rigid when full. It's one of those details you don't appreciate until you use it.

The lid seal is night and day. Souper Cubes lids snap on with an audible click and stay put. You can stack three or four filled trays in the freezer without worrying about them shifting or leaking. Walfos lids fit fine, but they're looser — enough that stacking can be precarious, and you'll occasionally find frost inside the lid.

Portion variety matters. The Souper Cubes set includes four different sizes: 2 cups (entree portion), 1 cup (side or soup bowl), ½ cup (sauce or rice side), and 2 tablespoons (garlic, pesto, tomato paste). This range makes the set genuinely useful for everything from full freezer meals to tiny ingredient portions. Walfos gives you four identical 1.5-cup trays — good for soups and sauces, but you lose the flexibility to portion small ingredients.

Real talk about silicone: Platinum-cured vs standard silicone is like cast iron vs non-stick. Both cook eggs. One lasts ten years. The other needs replacing. Souper Cubes uses the pro-grade material. Walfos uses the standard stuff. Both work — just know what you're paying for.

Where Walfos Wins

The price is almost unbelievable. At ~$25 for four trays with lids, Walfos costs less than a single Souper Cubes tray (which averages $19.75 per piece). If you're on a tight budget or just want to dip your toe into freezer meal prep, the Walfos set is a no-brainer. You get 6 cups of total capacity — actually more than Souper Cubes' 3.75 cups — at a fraction of the price.

More total freezing capacity. Four 1.5-cup trays give you 6 cups of total freezing space versus Souper Cubes' 3.75 cups. If your primary need is freezing large batches of soup or stock in uniform portions, Walfos actually delivers more usable volume per dollar.

Great for the "try it" crowd. If you're not sure whether silicone freezer molds will fit your lifestyle, spending $78.99 to find out is a big ask. At $25, the Walfos set is an easy impulse buy. Use them for six months, figure out what works, then upgrade to Souper Cubes if you're hooked.

The $54 Question

The price difference between these two sets is $54. Here's the breakdown of what that extra money actually buys you:

The cost-per-use calculation matters. If Souper Cubes last 5 years of weekly use (260 uses) and Walfos last 2 years (104 uses), here's the math:

  • Souper Cubes: $78.99 ÷ 260 uses = $0.30 per use
  • Walfos: $25.00 ÷ 104 uses = $0.24 per use

Surprisingly close. The upfront cost difference looks massive, but spread over the lifespan of each product, Souper Cubes is only marginally more expensive per use — and you get better lids, steel reinforcement, oven-safe capability, and four different portion sizes.

Where Walfos pulls ahead: If you're not sure you'll stick with meal prep, or you only freeze things occasionally, the Walfos set makes more sense. At $25, even if you use it for a year and move on, the cost is negligible.

The honest take: If you meal prep regularly — meaning at least twice a month — buy the Souper Cubes. The quality difference is real, and they'll last long enough that the $54 premium fades into insignificance. If you're trying meal prep for the first time or only freeze things once in a while, start with Walfos. You can always upgrade later.

Durability Over Time

We looked at user reviews after 6, 12, and 18 months of ownership for both products. The pattern is consistent:

Souper Cubes at 18 months: Still performing like new. Silicone is flexible, lids still snap tight, no discoloration or odor retention. Users report treating them roughly — dishwasher cycles, hot soup directly from the stove, stacking in an overstuffed freezer — and they hold up.

Walfos at 18 months: Mixed reviews. About 60% of users are still happy. The other 40% report the silicone stiffening, lids not sealing as well, or cracks forming at the flex points. At the price point, most still feel they got their money's worth, but it's clearly not a long-term solution.

Key longevity factor: The platinum-cured silicone in Souper Cubes resists the freeze-thaw fatigue that eventually kills standard silicone. Every time you freeze and release a portion, standard silicone undergoes micro-stress. After dozens of cycles, that stress accumulates. Platinum-cured silicone is more elastic and recovers better. This is physics, not marketing.

Which One Should You Buy?

The Bottom Line

For serious meal preppers: Get the Souper Cubes. They cost more upfront but deliver genuinely better materials (platinum-cured silicone), superior design (steel-reinforced rims, snap-on lids, fill lines, varied sizes), and significantly longer lifespan. At $0.30 per use over 5 years, they're actually a better value than they first appear.

For casual users and first-timers: Start with Walfos. At $25, it's a low-risk way to discover whether silicone freezer molds fit your kitchen routine. If you use them weekly for six months and wish they were better, you've validated the Souper Cubes upgrade. If they sit in a drawer, you're out $25 instead of $79.

Our pick: Souper Cubes. For anyone who actually meal preps with any regularity, the quality gap is worth the price. These things will outlast your current freezer.
